title: CPR – Child (1 year to puberty)
summary: For a child from about 1 year old to puberty who is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Compressions are one-third of the chest depth, about 5 cm.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} now and get an AED
when: Child unresponsive and not breathing normally – shout for help and call, phone on speaker
If you are alone with no phone and the collapse was not witnessed, give about 2 minutes of CPR before leaving to call (AHA)

steps.title: Check safety and response
steps.text: Tap the child and shout their name. Shout for help.

steps.title: Open the airway and check breathing
steps.text: Head tilt, chin lift. Look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
steps.caution: Local protocols differ: the European Resuscitation Council teaches 5 initial rescue breaths for a child before compressions. Follow the method you were trained in.

steps.title: Call {EMERGENCY} and send for an AED
Start chest compressions
steps.text: Heel of one hand (or two hands for a larger child) on the lower half of the breastbone.
points: Push down at least one-third of the chest depth – about 5 cm (2 in)

steps.title: Give rescue breaths
steps.text: If trained, give 2 breaths after every 30 compressions (one rescuer). Tilt head, lift chin, pinch nose, seal your mouth over theirs and breathe gently until the chest rises.
points: If you cannot give breaths, continue compressions only – but breaths are especially important for children

steps.title: Use an AED as soon as available
steps.text: Use child pads or the child setting if the AED has them; otherwise use adult pads, placed so they do not touch each other (front and back if necessary).

steps.title: Continue
steps.text: Keep going until help takes over or the child starts breathing normally. Then place them in the recovery position and keep checking breathing.

warningSigns: Very slow or absent breathing after choking, drowning or a seizure
doNot: Do not delay CPR to search for a pulse
Do not shake a child to wake them

sources.title: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
